jobs.title: Athletic and Youth Program Director
jobs.description:
Come join a dynamic and mission\-driven team at the growing YMCA of Greenwich!
Job Description
The Athletic and Youth Program Director is responsible for building, operating, and continuously improving the YMCA of Greenwich’s aquatic and youth programming portfolio. Acting as the Athletic Director for the YMCA’s competitive swim, dive, and water polo programs, this leader works in close partnership with head coaches to set program standards, drive team growth, and ensure that every athlete has a clear and supported path forward to reach their full potential. This role leads the full swim school operation from traditional lessons to community\-based offerings and competitive pathways while also overseeing the YMCA’s youth extracurricular programming and partnerships.


This position brings vision, operational discipline, and a genuine passion for youth development through sport and has the organizational development skills to build quality programs.


Qualifications
* Bachelor’s degree in sports management, recreation, physical education, nonprofit management, or a related field; equivalent experience considered.
* Minimum 5–7 years of progressive experience in aquatics, youth sports, or recreation program leadership.
* Demonstrated success managing multi\-program portfolios and leading teams.
* Strong financial acumen including experience building and managing budgets, driving enrollment revenue, and analyzing program performance.
* Deep knowledge of youth development principles, progressive skill\-building curricula, and structured youth enrichment operations.
* Experience working with or overseeing competitive sports programs and coaching staff strongly preferred.
  

Strong partnership development and community engagement skills.
* Excellent communication skills with participants, families, staff, and organizational leadership.
* Current CPR/AED and First Aid certification required.
* Familiarity with USA Swimming, US Diving, or USA Water Polo governance preferred.
Essential Functions
**Competitive Athletics – Swim, Dive and Water Polo**

* Serve as the Athletic Director for the YMCA’s competitive swim, dive, and water polo programs, providing strategic oversight, program direction, and organizational support to each team’s coaching staff.
* Partner closely with head coaches to set team goals, build program culture, establish athlete development standards, and ensure each competitive program reflects the values and mission of the YMCA.
* Build systems that support coach effectiveness and athlete experience, including scheduling, meet logistics, communication with families, and athlete recognition.
* Ensure competitive programs are properly resourced, staffed, and positioned for growth, identifying opportunities to expand participation, strengthen community relationships, and elevate the YMCA’s reputation as a destination for competitive aquatics.
* Champion the development of the whole athlete — ensuring every competitive participant grows not only in their sport but in leadership, character, and life skills that extend well beyond the pool.
Maintain compliance with all relevant governing body requirements (USA Swimming, USA Diving, USA Water Polo) and ensure coaches hold current and appropriate certifications for their sport.  
* 

  

**Youth Development Strategy \& Program Quality**

* Own the strategic direction, daily operations, and continuous improvement and growth of the YMCA’s full swim school program and community\-based aquatic initiatives.
* Establish and maintain program quality standards aligned with Red Cross WSI Swim Lesson curriculum and national best practices, ensuring a consistent and high\-quality experience for every participant at every level.
* Design and strengthen participant pathways that create a natural, well\-supported progression from foundational swim lessons through intermediate programming and into competitive aquatics for those who are ready.
* Analyze enrollment trends, session performance, and participant feedback to drive continuous improvement, identify growth opportunities, and ensure programming is responsive to community demand.
* Develop and lead adaptive programming to serve as an entry point into inclusive YMCA programming.
Partner with Marketing to communicate the swim school’s value proposition and impact, supporting enrollment growth through compelling storytelling and community visibility.  
*

* Develop, manage, and grow the YMCA’s youth extracurricular portfolio, with a focus on introductory and developmental programming that gives young people their first positive experience with organized athletics and enrichment programming.
* Build and steward partnerships with schools, youth sports organizations, and community groups to expand access, co\-develop programming, and grow the YMCA’s presence in the youth sports landscape.
Ensure all youth sports and extracurricular programs reflect the YMCA’s commitment to access, inclusion, and positive youth development, prioritizing participation, character, and skill\-building over competition at the introductory level.  
*

### **Program Director, Innovation Fellows Initiative, Cornell Tech (NYC)**


APPLY

 **About Cornell Tech**


Cornell Tech is Cornell University’s state\-of\-the\-art campus in New York City that develops leaders and technologies for the AI era through foundational and applied research, graduate education, and new ventures. Located on Roosevelt Island, the growing campus was founded in partnership with the Technion\-Israel Institute of Technology and in close collaboration with the NYC Economic Development Corporation after Cornell won a worldwide competition initiated by Mayor Michael R. Bloomberg’s administration to create an applied sciences campus in New York City. More than 1,000 Cornell students are now educated annually on the campus, including 700 in Cornell Tech programs. Since opening in 2012, nearly 120 new companies have spun out from startup programs at Cornell Tech, and 95 percent of them are based in New York City. Cornell Tech continues to have a transformative economic impact on the region’s tech sector.

 **About the Urban Tech Hub at Cornell Tech’s Jacob’s Institute**


The Urban Tech Hub at the Jacobs Institute at Cornell Tech is a pioneering academic center in New York City focused on transforming urban living through technology. We drive applied research, foster a dynamic tech ecosystem, and cultivate future urban technology leaders. Our mission is to develop responsible, human\-centered solutions that empower communities by expanding access to the tech sector and creating equitable opportunities for all.

  

We foster technological innovations that enhance city life—making cities smarter, more resilient, and more accessible for people and businesses. Our work bridges the gap between academic research and public need, forging strategic partnerships between academia, industry, local communities, and government to address urban challenges in real\-time.

  

Through collaborative research and hands\-on problem\-solving, we train the next generation of technologists to apply their skills in partnership with communities. Our projects, from AI to sustainability, tackle critical issues, ensuring that technological advancements improve lives and strengthen urban resilience. By working alongside diverse partners, from startups to municipal governments, the Hub aims to further the positive impact of urban technologies and help create stronger, fairer cities.

 **About the Jacobs Technion\-Cornell Institute**


The Jacobs Institute fosters radical experimentation at the intersection of research, education, and entrepreneurship. Established jointly by Cornell University and the Technion\-Israel Institute of Technology, our mission is to transform key industries through technological innovation, deep\-tech startups, and uniquely skilled talent.  



  

Launched in 2013 through a generous naming gift from Joan and Irwin Jacobs, the Joan and Irwin Jacobs Technion\-Cornell Institute embodies a bold experiment in graduate education, research, and entrepreneurship. The Jacobs Institute brings together engineers, computer scientists, designers, clinicians and entrepreneurs to develop new technologies, launch startups and generate real\-world impact through three research hubs focused on health, media and urban challenges and focuses on innovation that serves the digital age—offering dual\-degree programs, startup accelerators, and deep engagement with industry leaders in NYC and beyond. Research is supported through private philanthropy and competitive grants from U.S. government agencies.

**About Afghan Health Initiative**

Afghan Health Initiative (AHI) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to empowering immigrant and refugee communities through culturally and linguistically appropriate social services, educational support, and health and wellness resources. We strive to foster equitable access to opportunities that promote health, well\-being, and economic growth. Our mission is guided by a deep commitment to community\-centered care, cultural humility, and building trust with the people we serve.

**Position Overview**

The **Development Director** owns AHI’s overall development program, setting fundraising strategy, growing and diversifying revenue, and building the donor relationships and team capacity needed to sustain AHI’s mission over the long term. This position is ideal for a strategic fundraising leader who can set direction, build relationships at the highest level, and lead a development team.

Reporting to the Executive Director, the Development Director sets AHI’s annual and multi\-year fundraising strategy, manages a portfolio of major individual, corporate, and foundation donors, supervises development staff, and partners with the Executive Director and Board of Directors to grow AHI’s philanthropic capacity.

This role provides overall leadership for branch operations, staff development, branch council engagement, fundraising, financial performance, community impact, and participation in the planning and execution of the branch redevelopment.


As a key leader within the Association and the Kent County community, the Executive Director will balance strong day\-to\-day operating leadership with long\-range redevelopment planning. Working at GISB means being part of a school community where every role actively contributes to the overall experience of our students and families. As a private, mission\-driven institution, we place a strong emphasis on academic excellence, community, and relationships, with the goal of creating a school where students and families choose to join us and remain with us throughout their educational journey. We value colleagues who take initiative, collaborate across teams, and engage with the life of the school. This can take many forms, from participating in events and supporting school development to contributing ideas and experiences that strengthen our community.


The Director of Communications \& Advancement serves as a key leader within the administrative team, responsible for the strategic growth and long\-term sustainability of the School through communications, marketing, brand management, advancement, fundraising, donor engagement, and community outreach, with a strong focus on supporting the recruitment and retention of families.


This is a highly visible, hands\-on leadership role that combines strategic planning with day\-to\-day execution. The Director develops and implements the School’s communications, marketing, and advancement strategies while actively writing communications, creating campaigns and content, strengthening the School’s brand and visibility, and supporting fundraising and donor engagement.


Working closely with the Head of Administration, Head of School, and Director of Enrollment Management \& Alumni Relations, the Director ensures that communications and advancement efforts support the School’s strategic priorities, strengthen community engagement, and contribute directly to family recruitment and retention and long\-term sustainability.


The Director supervises the Marketing \& Design Coordinator and leads the School’s communications and advancement functions. This role requires a creative, relationship\-driven leader who can move easily between strategy and execution, tell the School’s story effectively, build strong relationships, and actively engage with families, donors, alumni, and the broader Greater Boston community.

**Responsibilities:**

**Communications \& Digital Strategy**

* Develop, implement, and continuously improve the school's communication strategy, standards, and workflows to ensure clear, timely, consistent, and mission\-aligned communication across the organization.
* Create, write, edit, and publish internal and external communications, including newsletters, publications, website content, press releases, executive communications, and crisis communications.
* Lead the implementation, administration, and continuous improvement of school\-wide communication platforms and systems, including ParentSquare and future communication technologies.
* Implement and maintain the GISB Communication Handbook, communication standards, templates, and best practices across the School.
* Partner with school leaders and departments to improve communication workflows, responsiveness, and the overall family communication experience.
* Coordinate the school's communication and stakeholder feedback surveys in collaboration with the Head of Administration and the Director of Enrollment Management \& Alumni Relations, including annual satisfaction surveys, Net Promoter Score (NPS) surveys, new family surveys, exit surveys, and other feedback initiatives. Analyze results and implement communication improvements that strengthen transparency, consistency, responsiveness, and community trust.

* Create and manage content across digital and print platforms, including photography, videography, publications, advertising, presentations, brochures, and other marketing materials.
* Actively capture, write, edit, and publish authentic stories that showcase students, faculty, programs, and community life.
* Maintain the school's photography, video, and digital asset library for ongoing marketing and communication needs.
* Plan and execute major branding initiatives, website enhancements, anniversary campaigns, and other strategic communication projects.

**Advancement \& Donor Relations**

jobs.description:
**Position:** Senior Vice President of Development

**Location:** Columbia, SC

**About Presbyterian Communities of South Carolina (PCSC)**


PCSC is a compassionate Christian ministry dedicated to enriching the quality of life for seniors of all faiths. We do this by owning and operating six Life Plan retirement communities across the state. Our longstanding mission guides our work, our relationships, and our commitment to excellence across all communities we serve. We enjoy close, supportive relationships with the Presbyterian churches in the state and denominational affiliates. The PCSC Foundation is a 501(c)(3\) charitable Type I organization that supports the mission of PCSC.

**Position Summary**


The Senior Vice President of Development serves as the executive leader responsible for PCSC’s fundraising strategy, outcomes, and the overall direction of the PCSC Foundation. This newly created position reports to the CEO and represents a significant organizational investment in the growth, visibility, and impact of philanthropy across PCSC.


As a member of the core executive leadership team, the Senior Vice President provides high\-level guidance for PCSC’s philanthropic initiatives, serves as the primary spokesperson for fundraising, and oversees the strategic development, alignment, and performance of the Foundation. This role is a senior leadership position with substantial influence and decision\-making responsibilities focused on the philanthropic priorities of PCSC.

**Key Responsibilities include but limited to:**

*Strategic Fundraising Leadership*

* Develop and execute long\-term philanthropic strategy to increase charitable giving, planned gifts, and donor engagement.
* Lead the vision, design, and execution of major funds, annual fundraising priorities, and capital campaigns.
* Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward major donor prospects statewide (including residents and their families) through personal visits, relationship\-building, and strategic engagement.
* Ensure appropriate donor recognition, including plaques, naming opportunities, and dedication events.

*Planned Giving*

* Grow and manage a robust planned giving program that includes bequests, legacy gifts, and charitable estate commitments.
* Promote planned giving through educational outreach, donor conversations, and strategic communication materials.

*Church and Community Relations*

* Support and direct staff tasked with maintaining strong relationships with Presbyterian Church (USA) congregations, ministers, presbyteries, and church leaders throughout South Carolina.
* Present mission\-centered programs to civic groups and lay groups.
* Maintain a highly visible presence on PCSC campuses through regular visits, events, and interaction with residents, families, and staff.

*Board Relations and Foundation Oversight*

* Present reports to, and collaborate with, the Foundation’s Board of Directors; Present reports to, and participate in, PCSC Board of Trustee meetings.
* Provide executive oversight for Foundation operations, staffing, and budget management. Supervise the Director of Annual Giving and Church Relations, as well as the Foundation Assistant.
* Ensure donor records, gift acknowledgments, and financial stewardship practices are accurate, timely, and aligned with donor intent.
* Collaborate with the CEO and CFO to ensure the Foundation’s investment manager supports the long\-term philanthropic goals of PCSC.
* Oversee communications related to philanthropy, church relations, and donor publications.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree required.
* Minimum five years of fundraising or funds development experience.
* Demonstrated experience working effectively with faith\-based organizations.
* Strong proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and willingness to develop intermediate skills with Raiser’s Edge NXT.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Seven years of fundraising experience, including planned giving.
* Proven positive working relationships with Presbyterian Church (USA) congregations.
* Professional fundraising certification (e.g., CFRE) preferred.

**Ideal Candidate Attributes:**

* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Strong leadership, initiative, and delegation capability.
* Ability to plan, organize, and manage time effectively.
* Demonstrated stewardship of financial and human resources.
* Knowledge of legal and tax aspects of planned giving suitable to the role.

**Benefits:**


We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes competitive paid time off, medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 403(b)\-retirement plan with employer matching, and opportunities for professional growth and leadership development.

**Apply Today** to be a part of organization that serves the residents with excellence through healthy relationships, teamwork, and Stewardship

jobs.description:
**Job Summary:**
  

The Executive Director, Federal Government Relations \- D.C. Office serves as a senior federal advocate responsible for advancing Kaiser Permanentes federal legislative agenda. Reporting to the Vice President, Federal Government Relations, this role leads advocacy strategies across an assigned portfolio of enterprise priorities and represents Kaiser Permanente before Congress, congressional committees, and other key federal stakeholders.  

  

The Executive Director is a senior lobbyist responsible for developing and executing comprehensive advocacy strategies that build congressional support for Kaiser Permanentes policy objectives. Working in close partnership with policy leaders, public affairs, and internal stakeholders, this position translates organizational priorities into coordinated federal engagement strategies that advance Kaiser Permanentes integrated, value\-based care model.  

  

The ideal candidate is a strategic, mission\-driven government relations leader with deep knowledge of the federal legislative process and established credibility on Capitol Hill. This individual must understand and champion Kaiser Permanentes commitment to high\-quality, affordable, equitable, and prevention\-focused health care, and effectively communicate the organizations policy positions to lawmakers, congressional staff, trade associations, coalition partners, and external stakeholders.  

  

Based in Washington, D.C., the Executive Director develops and maintains senior relationships with Members of Congress, committee staff, and key external organizations aligned with assigned issue priorities. This role leads lobbying efforts on the organizations highest\-priority federal issues, coordinates advocacy strategies across relevant trade associations and coalitions, and partners closely with colleagues across Kaiser Permanente to ensure consistent, enterprise\-wide alignment on legislative priorities.  

  

The Executive Director also provides leadership and mentorship to assigned staff, manages approximately one to two direct reports, and contributes to the continued growth and effectiveness of Kaiser Permanentes federal affairs function through collaboration, strategic insight, and operational excellence.  

**Essential Responsibilities:**  

  

* Lead the development and execution of comprehensive federal advocacy strategies for an assigned portfolio of Kaiser Permanentes highest\-priority legislative issues.
* Serve as a senior advocate before Congress, congressional committees, and other federal policymakers on assigned issue priorities.
* Develop and maintain strategic relationships with Members of Congress, senior congressional staff, committee staff, and key Administration officials.
* Support Kaiser Permanentes engagement with national trade associations, coalitions, and external stakeholders aligned with assigned legislative priorities.
* Identify legislative opportunities and risks, develop advocacy strategies, and recommend courses of action to advance enterprise objectives.
* Partner with Policy, Public Affairs, Permanente Medical Groups, Risant Health, and other enterprise leaders to ensure alignment on federal legislative priorities and advocacy strategies.
* Provide strategic counsel and policy updates to senior leaders regarding congressional activity, political developments, and legislative strategy.
* Develop congressional champions and expand Kaiser Permanentes influence with key policymakers and stakeholders.
* Supervise, coach, and develop assigned Directors while fostering a collaborative, high\-performing advocacy team.
* Represent Kaiser Permanente at congressional hearings, stakeholder meetings, conferences, and other external events.
* Support the Vice President in advancing departmental priorities, strategic initiatives, and organizational objectives.
* Ensure advocacy activities are conducted in compliance with all applicable lobbying disclosure and ethics requirements.

 **Basic Qualifications:**
Experience* Minimum twelve (12\) years of relevant professional experience.
* Minimum ten (10\) years of progressively responsible experience in federal, state, or local government relations, legislative affairs, health policy, public affairs, communications, or a closely related field.
* Minimum five (5\) years of experience leading complex advocacy initiatives, government relations functions, teams, or high\-profile legislative campaigns.


Education* Bachelors degree from an accredited college or university or four (4\) years of experience in a directly related field required.
* High School Diploma or General Education Development (GED) required.


License, Certification, Registration* N/A


**Additional Requirements:*** Demonstrated success developing and executing legislative advocacy strategies, influencing public policy outcomes, and building trusted relationships with Members of Congress, congressional committees, federal agencies, trade associations, and other external stakeholders.

**Preferred Qualifications:*** Significant experience advocating on federal health care policy issues.
* Experience working with Congress, the Executive Branch, a national health care organization, trade association, congressional office, or federal agency.
* Demonstrated experience advising senior executives on legislative strategy, political developments, and advocacy priorities.
* Experience leading cross\-functional teams and building consensus across complex organizations.

The Wisconsin Foundation and Alumni Association (WFAA), the private fundraising and alumni relations organization for the University of Wisconsin–Madison, is seeking a relationship\-driven and strategic Director of Development, Foundation Relations to support the College of Engineering.This role is ideal for a collaborative fundraiser who enjoys connecting innovative academic and research priorities with philanthropic foundations that want to make a meaningful impact.  

In this role, you will build, manage, and steward strategic relationships with philanthropic foundations to advance the academic, research, and engagement priorities of the College of Engineering. You will work closely with college leadership, faculty, staff, and WFAA colleagues to identify funding opportunities, develop compelling proposals, and communicate the impact of foundation support. This position will be a combination of remote, in\-office, and on\-site work environments. **Who is WFAA?**  

The Wisconsin Foundation and Alumni Association is a private, nonprofit corporation that encourages individuals and organizations to make gifts to the university and to connect with the UW. In 2014, the UW Foundation merged with the Wisconsin Alumni Association® to better serve a growing population of UW alumni and donors. We believe that private support grows out of good relationships between campus leaders, faculty, and program staff who need support, and the alumni and friends who want to invest in UW–Madison. We provide important engagement opportunities to link UW–Madison alumni to each other and to their alma mater, building a strong community of Badgers. **Diversity and Inclusion:**
Just as the university community benefits from differing viewpoints, perspectives, and experiences, inclusion and diversity are imperative for the success of our mission. WFAA values people and the differences that they bring to the organization, and creates an environment in which all staff members and constituents feel respected and have opportunities to thrive.
Essential Functions:
* Identifying and cultivating new relationships with foundations that support the programming and research goals of the College and its constituent departments and schools;
* Coordinating, managing and advancing existing relationships with external foundation funding partners;
* Developing strong collaborative partnerships with internal and external stakeholders and leveraging those relationships to result in successful funding opportunities;
* Working with the dean, associate deans, department chairs, faculty, and staff to identify, develop, and submit funding proposals;
* Facilitating stewardship of awarded funds, including required reporting by funding partners and communicating research and programming impact to internal and external stakeholders;
* Creating and presenting concise, readily understood presentations of complex materials;
* Maintaining knowledge of current best practices and trends in foundation\-based philanthropy;
* Successfully articulating department and College research and programming priorities to internal and external stakeholders;
* Understanding and accessing resources within WFAA to support the fund development process.
